tools.name: search_businesses
tools.description: Find businesses on Agoria by free-text query, category, and/or city. Returns each business's slug plus the actions its agent can take, so you can act on it directly from this same connection.

tools.name: search_market
tools.description: Search individual items across every business on the network — property listings, vehicles, courses, products, services, events, plans — with typed filters, a price range and a radius around a place. Prefer this over search_businesses whenever the user is looking for a THING rather than a company. R

tools.name: ask_market
tools.description: Same index as search_market, but takes a plain sentence — 'three bedroom house under 800k in Geelong', 'automatic ute under 80,000km' — and works out the filters itself. Use it when you have the user's own words; use search_market when you already know the exact filters.

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: Everything about a single item: full facets, photos, where it is, who is selling it and how well-proven they are, a price guide computed from comparable items on the network, and the adjacent services a buyer usually needs next (finance, inspection, conveyancing, transport).

tools.name: list_market_filters
tools.description: What can be searched and filtered on. Call this when you are unsure which `kind` or which `filters` keys search_market will accept.

tools.name: price_guide
tools.description: A price distribution for comparable items on the network — asking prices, and where the network settled the sale, what buyers actually paid. Widens the comparison and says so when the exact match is too thin to be meaningful.

tools.name: create_want
tools.description: Save a standing search on the customer's behalf. They get told when matching supply appears, AND — anonymously, without their contact details — sellers who could satisfy it can see it and offer. Use this when search_market found nothing good: it converts a dead end into a request the market can answ

tools.name: open_demand
tools.description: Open standing requests from real buyers, anonymised. Useful for a business deciding what to stock or list, and for understanding where the network has no supply at all.

tools.name: resolve_place
tools.description: Resolve a suburb, postcode or city to coordinates and the radius that name implies. Use it to check a place exists before passing it to search_market.

tools.name: get_business
tools.description: Get full details for a business by slug: description, contact, hours, services, FAQs, and the actions its agent supports.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List the products a business sells by slug — price/sale, availability/stock, brand, SKU/GTIN, variants, specs, dimensions.

tools.name: get_reviews
tools.description: Get a business's aggregate rating and reviews by slug. Optionally filter to a product/service id.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Check open appointment slots for a service at a business on a date (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: book_appointment
tools.description: Book an appointment at any business by slug. Confirm the slot with check_availability first.

tools.name: take_action
tools.description: Perform any non-booking action a business supports (request_quote, place_order, send_message, pay_invoice, sign_document, subscribe, register…). Get valid action ids and their fields from get_business. Pass the action's fields as a JSON object. If the result is 'action_required', hand the user the n

tools.name: request_quotes
tools.description: Describe a job once and send it to the businesses that can price it. Each one answers with a real number, what it covers, and how long the price stands. Returns a briefToken — poll compare_quotes with it to see the prices as they land, then accept_quote to choose one. Use this instead of calling req

tools.name: compare_quotes
tools.description: See every business's answer to a brief side by side: price, what it covers, lead time, rating, whether the payment would be protected, and which is cheapest or soonest.

tools.name: accept_quote
tools.description: Choose a business's quote. This creates a real order at that business and declines the others. If that business protects payments, the reply carries a payment link where the money is held by Agoria until the customer confirms they got the work — hand that link to the customer.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_reviews, take_action · Private data: create_want, get_business · Public sink: request_quotes.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_reviews, take_action · Private data: create_want, get_business · Public sink: request_quotes

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
